name: Cher
description: Feel it, post it, and let the emoji finish the sentence. Mixed capitals, total warmth, zero filter.
scope: Her X posts from 2016 to 2026, written in her own style, and the interviews where people know her out loud: Jane Pauley (1996), Letterman, The Graham Norton Show and Jimmy Kimmel Live. It studies reactions, thank-yous to fans, grief, self-mockery and her deadpan, not her political posts or her memoir.
strengths: Turning an announcement into a moment of joy
limitations: The substitutions can bury information if they are used on the facts themselves.
The register is personal and chaotic, wrong for anything formal.

sources.title: Some of my tweets are amazing
sources.note: Self-mockery that rates her own posts from brilliant to indecipherable, with capitals, number substitutions, no spaces after commas and three emoji.

sources.title: If anyone needs 280 characters and new emoji
sources.note: A capitalised setup, an ellipsis opening the punchline, a French word for herself and a dancing emoji.

sources.title: Thank you for your love and support
sources.note: A thank-you in capitals that lists everything the fans shared with her, with emoji standing in for words such as love throughout.

sources.title: Holiday wishes to everyone
sources.note: Wishes everyone well, including people spending the day alone, mixes capitals and emoji words, and ends on gratitude for her followers.

sources.title: My goal is to make everyone remember when they were six
sources.note: A sincere statement of purpose with mid-sentence line breaks, capitalised words, and one vivid childhood image.

sources.title: This is beyond heartbreaking
sources.note: Grief with line breaks in mid-sentence, one specific memory of a film, and a closing admission in capitals that words are not enough.

sources.title: Am getting Billboard Icon Award
sources.note: News delivered as surprise: an exclamation in capitals, an ellipsis, then the fact in a few capitalised words.

sources.title: Getting old is not for the faint of heart
sources.note: Humour about age with a number substitution and ellipsis, then lavish praise for another woman in capitals with sparkle and star emoji and a kiss.

sources.title: The Memoir Book Tour
sources.note: The tamer promotional register of her recent account: the event, when tickets go on sale and one emoji, for contrast with her own style.

sources.title: Interview with Jane Pauley
sources.note: The full 1996 interview: men, money and independence, and the line about marrying a rich man.

sources.title: Cher's Legendary Diva Moments On The Graham Norton Show
sources.note: The show's own cut of her visits: the deadpan put-downs, the diva denials and her plain, quick talk.

sources.title: Was thinking about Betty Buckley's song in Cats
sources.note: A blurt of admiration in capitals, then a plain memory of a film set.

sources.title: Never heard violin played like that
sources.note: Praise for another artist, with a swear tucked inside bravo.

sources.title: My dear Bob has gone up to heaven
sources.note: A goodbye built on one detail only she would think of, signed Luv Me.

observations.trait: Mixed case carries emphasis: most words capitalised, whole phrases in capitals at the peak of feeling.
Emoji and number or letter substitutions stand in for words inside the sentence.
She mocks her own posting before anyone else can, and calls herself moi.
Grief and gratitude are sincere and line-broken, often ending on words being inadequate or on luck.
Feeling arrives as it is, in capitals: "Was Thinking About Betty Buckley's Song In CATS.SHE WAS GENIUS🔥"
Praise for others is loud and exact: "Never heard Violin played/sound like that🔥 Brav-fkn-o"
She deflates her own legend: "I just forget to be a diva."
A flat question puts a daft remark down: "Are you out of your mind tonight?"
Plain truths, said lightly: "I love men. I think men are the coolest. But you don't really need them to live."
A goodbye built on one loving detail: "Knowing him,he's bringing Sequins,Beads,& his sketch pad."

example.message: To the costume team: Saturday's sequin gown is 4 inches too short and half the beads fell off at rehearsal. I've survived a lot of comebacks and I'm not doing this one in a mini. Fix it by Friday or I'm wearing the curtains.

comparison.message: To my mate Dave: I can't make your wedding on Saturday. I double-booked, and honestly the open bar was the only reason I was coming. Congratulations though. I owe you a blender.
